steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ How can the coordinates of the randomWallTile be used in the setTileAt function?


Solution:

The coordinate parameters in the setTileAt function should be changed to (randomWallTile.column, randomWallTile.row).

Ask the ninja: 

❓What function will stop the Player sprite from moving through box tiles?


Solution:

Code should be added to set wall on where the boxTile is placed on the tilemap: tiles.setWallAt(tiles.getTileLocation(randomWallTile.column, randomWallTile.row), true) inside the onUpdateInterval function.


Ask the ninja: 

❓ How can you check the length of an array of a specific tile?


Solution:

The floorTile asset code should be added inside the parentheses of the getTilesByType function, followed by a dot operator and length. The code inside the parentheses of the if conditional should look like:

tiles.getTilesByType(assets.tile`floorTile`.length == 0.
steps.instructions:
Fix the bugs in the code to create a working tilemap project with walls!


The exit tile should be placed on the random wall tile selected from the wallTileList array, each time the project starts.


The Player sprite should not be able to overlap box tiles when they appear on the tilemap.


If there are no more floor tiles on the tilemap, the project should end in a loss.


Use the functions in the code menu, the debug tool, and the code completion tool to create a working version of this tilemap project with walls!

subgroups.title: Debugging Tilemap Walls
subgroups.introduction: Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!

validationItems.text: setTileAt, setWallAt, and getTilesByType functions updated

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 2 of Brown Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about tilemap overlap events and how to make different things happen when sprites overlap different tiles and walls. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 2:

badges.title: The Big Event
badges.description: Use events to control what happens to sprites navigating a tilemap in a project in JavaScript.

badges.title: Touch Controls
badges.description: Make something happen when a sprite overlaps a specific tile.

badges.title: A Chain of Reactions
badges.description: Make something happen when a sprite hits a wall.

badges.title: A Glyph in the System
badges.description: Use an image asset as a cursor image in a dialog box.

badges.title: Save for Later
badges.description: Create an array to store all of the locations of a specific tile type on a tilemap.

badges.title: Invisible Walls
badges.description: Turn a wall on or off at a specific location on a tilemap.
